required_fixes: Fix client to actually exercise HTTP conditional caching: run_experiment.py never sends If-None-Match header, so mock_server.py If-None-Match -> 304 code path (research/experiments/EXP-GRAPH-35375596525/mock_server.py:460-467) is never exercised. Conditional GET must be implemented and 304 rate logged as manipulation check. Current evidence tests only declarative Cache-Control/ETag headers, not operational 304 behavior.

Log realized cache hit rate, ETag match rate, and actual I/O latency distribution as artifacts. Prereg section 18 threat 5 and result.json unresolved explicitly list these as unlogged; without them the controlled difference 'HTTP caching enabled vs disabled' cannot be quantified (result.json:unresolved[5], report.md:Validity Threats 5).

Increase n to match parent power or correct power claim: n=240 gives SE=0.06496 and minimum detectable |r|=0.1266 (result.json:metrics:power_analysis:min_detectable_r_at_n) and 95% CI half-width ~0.127 in r-space. Parent n=480 gave SE=0.0458 and CI upper 0.135 at r=0.046. The CI widening from 0.135 to 0.237 is partly sample-size artifact, not solely HTTP caching effect. Prereg power analysis assumed delta=0.15 equivalence powered at n=240 if |r|<0.129, but observed |r|=0.114 still yields CI upper 0.237 >0.15, showing assumption was optimistic. Match parent n=480 or pre-specify n for equivalence at expected r~0.05.

Fix decision-rule branching in run_experiment.py:566-577 so CI upper >=0.20 maps to FALSIFIES per spec.json decision_rule. Current code orders 'abs_r <0.15 and ci_upper>=0.15 -> MIXED' before 'ci_upper>=0.20 -> FALSIFIES', making FALSIFIES unreachable when abs_r<0.15 (observed abs_r=0.114, ci_upper=0.237 incorrectly yields MIXED instead of spec-intended FAIL/FALSIFIES for >=0.20). Report correctly notes FAIL but outcome field is MIXED.

Separate HTTP Cache-Control (max-age=5 / no-store) from in-memory SchemaCache TTL=0.5s in measurement: mock_server.py:439-452 SchemaCache TTL triggers independently of HTTP header; run_experiment.py toggles only header via /admin/set_caching but schema staleness is driven by TTL expiry, so the two layers are confounded. Log which layer served each /schema response (cached flag already in response but not persisted in raw_evidence) to isolate HTTP effect.

validity_findings.finding: HTTP caching manipulation as preregistered (Cache-Control + ETag + If-None-Match + 304) was not operationally exercised. run_experiment.py:get_schema and all request paths never set If-None-Match header; mock_server.py checks If-None-Match only when header present. Raw evidence contains no 304 responses and no ETag validation. Only Cache-Control header presence and ETag generation are tested; actual conditional caching (304 Not Modified) is untested. This limits causal attribution of any correlation change to HTTP caching.
validity_findings.evidence: research/experiments/EXP-GRAPH-35375596525/run_experiment.py:164-172 get_schema (no If-None-Match), research/experiments/EXP-GRAPH-35375596525/mock_server.py:460-467 If-None-Match handling, research/experiments/EXP-GRAPH-35375596525/raw_evidence/experiment_data.json (no 304 or cached flag persisted)

validity_findings.finding: Cache-Control max-age=5 vs no-store does not produce client-side caching because client issues unconditional GET each time. Server still returns 200 with fresh body computed via SchemaCache TTL=0.5s. The declared HTTP semantics are declarative only; no hit/miss behavior is enforced. Prereg measurement_validity items 2,9-10 describe HTTP elements but evidence shows they do not alter data flow.

At n=240, CI width is ~0.25 (observed CI [-0.0128,0.2372] width 0.25). To confirm |r|<0.15 with 95% CI upper <0.15, point estimate must be <~0.02 (since half-width ~0.127). Observed pooled r=0.114 is below 0.15 but CI fails due to variance, not systematic correlation. Power analysis min_detectable_r=0.1266 > observed 0.114 confirms underpowered for point estimate, and equivalence-powered claim in prereg section 12 (powered for delta=0.15 if observed |r|<0.129) was miscalibrated. Result is indeterminate between true orthogonality and insufficient n, not evidence HTTP caching breaks orthogonality.

Per-caching-mode correlations are heterogeneous and opposite to hypothesis: cache_enabled r=-0.0055 (95% CI [-0.185,0.174], TOST p_upper=0.045 PASS at delta=0.15) vs cache_disabled r=0.217 (95% CI [0.039,0.381], TOST p_upper=0.773 FAIL). Pooling obscures moderation. HTTP caching enabled *reduces* correlation (toward zero), disabled increases it. Hypothesis predicted caching introduces common cause and raises |r|; data show the opposite. Heterogeneity suggests sampling noise or unmodeled interaction, not systematic coupling.

baseline_findings.expected: Parent CI upper 0.135 <0.15 PASS at n=480 r=0.0463
baseline_findings.observed: Current pooled r=0.114 CI upper 0.237 >0.15 FAIL at n=240. Recomputed matches producer (r=0.11399, SE=0.06496, CI [-0.0128,0.2372], TOST p_upper=0.286). Increase in point estimate (+0.068) and CI upper (+0.102) partly explained by halved n (SE increase 0.0458->0.065, expected CI width +0.038) and partly by higher observed r. Cache_enabled subset alone (r=-0.0055 CI upper 0.174) still > parent 0.135 but TOST passes at delta=0.15 (p=0.045), showing HTTP header presence alone does not materially break orthogonality beyond sampling variation.
baseline_findings.assessment: Baseline comparison correctly isolates sample-size confound. Parent superiority is not solely HTTP caching effect; underpowered design inflates CI. Isolated HTTP effect (cache_enabled vs disabled) shows no systematic coupling attributable to headers.

claim_ceiling: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 is NOT confirmed on this evidence: pooled r=0.114, 95% CI [-0.013,0.237], CI upper 0.237 >=0.15, TOST p_upper=0.286 FAIL (result.json:controls:C3_equivalence, report.md:Executive Summary). Producer's negative conclusion (C1 PASS, C2 4/4 PASS, C4 FP=0 PASS, C3 FAIL -> outcome MIXED/ overall FAIL) is measurement-valid and recomputed exactly. However, the maximum justified causal claim is bounded to: n=240 localhost Flask 3.1.3 + SQLite WAL + TTL=0.5s + jitter 10-100ms + HS256/RS256 with declarative HTTP cache headers (Cache-Control max-age=5/no-store, ETag SHA-256 generation) but WITHOUT operational conditional GET/304 exercise and without quantified cache hit rate. This is header-only, not full HTTP caching/CDN. The observed CI widening vs parent (0.135->0.237) is partly sample-size artifact (n 480->240) and partly higher point estimate, not attributable to HTTP caching as common cause; cache_enabled subset alone is near-zero (r=-0.0055, TOST PASS p=0.045) while cache_disabled is higher (r=0.217). No evidence HTTP caching introduces systematic behavioral-structural coupling; result is indeterminate due to underpowering and incomplete manipulation. Do NOT infer HTTP caching breaks parallel-channel architecture; do NOT promote to VALIDATED/PRODUCT_CORE; parallel channels remain EXPERIMENTAL bounded to stochastic mock without full HTTP caching. Next test must operationally exercise 304 and match parent n before attributing to caching.
unresolved: Whether orthogonality holds on real external APIs with production databases, distributed caches/CDN, network latency, OAuth/OIDC middleware, and production session stores — the parent carry_forward highest-upside question remains untested (spec explicitly bounds claim to localhost mock).
Whether delta=0.10 is practically required for product architecture vs delta=0.15 sufficient; this experiment underpowered for delta=0.10 and fails even at delta=0.15 due to n=240.
Whether per-caching heterogeneity (cache_enabled -0.005 vs disabled 0.217) is systematic moderation or sampling noise; requires replication at n=480 with operational 304.
Whether concurrent client load, cache invalidation/purge, stale-while-revalidate, or distributed cache coherence changes correlation structure — not tested.
Realized cache hit rate, ETag match rate, and latency distribution not logged, so cannot quantify stochasticity actually realized (result.json:unresolved[5]).
